source_text: Non mihi tam bene est, immo non mihi tam male est, ut apostolos committam. Sed quoniam perversissimi isti illam reprehensionem ad hoc obtendunt, ut suspectam faciant doctrinam superiorem, respondebo quasi pro Petro, ipsum Paulum dixisse factum se esse omnibus omnia, Iudaeis Iudaeum, non Iudaeis non Iudaeum, ut omnes lucrificaret. Adeo pro temporibus et personis et causis quaedam reprehendebant, in quae et ipsi aeque pro temporibus et personis et causis committebant, quemadmodum si et Petrus reprehenderet Paulum, quod prohibens circumcisionem circumcideret ipse Timotheum. Viderint qui de apostolis iudicant. Bene, quod Petrus Paulo et in martyrio adaequatur, Sed etsi in tertium usque caelum ereptus Paulus et in paradisum delatus audiit quaedam illic, non possunt videri fuisse quae illum in aliam doctrinam instructiorem praestarent, cum ita fuerit condicio eorum, ut nulli hominum proderentur. Quodsi ad alicuius conscientiam manavit nescio quid illud, et hoc se aliqua haeresis sequi affirmat, aut Paulus secreti proditi reus est, aut et alius postea in paradisum ereptus debet ostendi, cui permissum sit eloqui quae Paulo mutire non licuit.
thought_title: Paul's accommodation does not prove a hidden doctrine
orientation: Tertullian is answering heretics who use Peter's rebuke to make the earlier apostolic teaching suspect, and he now defends Paul's conduct and the public nature of apostolic doctrine.
pass_a_gloss: It is not so well with me, or rather it is not so badly with me, that I would set the apostles against one another. But since those most perverse people put forward that rebuke for this purpose, to make the earlier teaching suspect, I will answer as if on behalf of Peter, that Paul himself said that he had become all things to all people, to the Jews a Jew, to those not Jews one not a Jew, so that he might gain all. To such an extent they used to find fault with certain things according to times and persons and causes, into which they themselves equally according to times and persons and causes used to fall, just as if Peter also were to find fault with Paul, because while forbidding circumcision he himself circumcised Timothy. Let those who judge the apostles see to it. It is well that Peter is made equal to Paul even in martyrdom. But even if Paul was caught up to the third heaven and brought into paradise and heard certain things there, those things cannot be seen to have been such as would make him more fully instructed for another doctrine, since the condition of those things was such that they were disclosed to no human being. But if something of that kind leaked out to someone's knowledge, and some heresy claims that it follows this, either Paul is guilty of having divulged a secret, or another person must be shown to have been caught up into paradise afterwards, to whom it was permitted to speak out what Paul was not allowed to mutter.

pass_b_english: I have no desire—indeed, it is far from my intent—to set the apostles against one another. But since those most perverse people put forward that rebuke as a pretext to make the earlier teaching suspect, I will answer as if for Peter: Paul himself said that he had become all things to all people, a Jew to Jews and a non-Jew to non-Jews, so that he might win over everyone (1 Corinthians 9:20-22). So they found fault with certain things according to the times, the persons, and the circumstances, and they themselves equally committed those same things according to the times, the persons, and the circumstances—just as if Peter had rebuked Paul because, while forbidding circumcision, Paul himself circumcised Timothy (Acts 16:3). Let those who judge the apostles see to it. It is well that Peter is made equal to Paul even in martyrdom. But even if Paul was caught up to the third heaven and carried into paradise and heard certain things there, those things cannot be thought to have been such as would make him more fully instructed for another doctrine, since their condition was such that they were not to be disclosed to any human being (2 Corinthians 12:2-4). But if something of that kind leaked out to someone's knowledge, and some heresy claims to follow it, then either Paul is guilty of betraying a secret, or someone else must be shown to have been caught up into paradise afterward, to whom it was permitted to speak aloud what Paul was not allowed to whisper.

problems.quote: It is not so well with me, or rather it is not so badly with me, that I would set the apostles against one another.
problems.why: Double negative and contradictory phrasing ('not so well' / 'not so badly') makes the sentence nearly unreadable.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'I have no desire—indeed, it is far from my intent—to set the apostles against one another.'

edits.old: It is not so well with me, or rather it is not so badly with me, that I would set the apostles against one another.
edits.new: I have no desire—indeed, it is far from my intent—to set the apostles against one another.

fixed: The source reads 'Non mihi tam bene est, immo non mihi tam male est, ut apostolos committam.' The English 'It is not so well with me, or rather it is not so badly with me' is a literal rendering that is confusing in English. The suggested rewrite captures the sense ('I have no desire—indeed, it is far from my intent—to set the apostles against one another') while remaining literary and natural.
